biography: Jimmy "Hollywood" Means didn't come from racing royalty. He clawed his way from the dusty short tracks of rural Alabama, where his daddy ran a junkyard and taught him how to coax every last ounce of speed from busted-up stock cars. His first big break came at 19, qualifying for a regional Stock USA Gen1 race on a shoestring budget – his car held together with duct tape and sheer willpower. A daring last-lap pass for 5th place caught the eye of a small team owner, launching his professional career. Now, at 24, Jimmy's known for his aggressive driving and flamboyant personality, making him a fan favorite. He's currently battling for championship contention, aiming to prove he's more than just a flash in the pan.
drivingStyle: Means is a high-risk, high-reward driver. He attacks every corner with a "never lift" mentality, often pushing his car – and his tires – to the absolute limit. While this aggressive style leads to spectacular overtakes and thrilling finishes, it also makes him prone to mistakes. Tire management isn't his strong suit, but he compensates with sheer car control and an uncanny ability to hustle a wounded machine. When the pressure's on, Jimmy thrives, often pulling off improbable feats of skill and daring.

rivalries.reason: A clash of styles – Eldridge is a calculated strategist, while Means relies on raw aggression. Their contrasting approaches often lead to on-track battles and heated exchanges.
A rivalry born from a controversial incident at Daytona, where Means' aggressive block sent Rossi spinning. She hasn't forgotten, and seeks every opportunity for payback.
Harrison believes that Means' flashy persona is bad for the sport and has tried to put him in his place on and off the track. This has only fueled the rivalry.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of racing socks, regardless of the weather.
Listens to a specific blues song ('Crossroads' by Robert Johnson) before every race.
Always spins the tires exactly three times before pulling onto the track for qualifying.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser."
careerHighlight: Winning the Talladega 500 after starting from the back of the pack. He weaved through the field with a series of daring maneuvers, taking the lead on the final lap in a photo finish.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the championship-deciding race at Homestead due to an overly aggressive move, costing him his first title.
